outcome: intrapartum interventions (fetal scalp electrodes, intrauterine pressure catheters, epidural analgesia, fetal scalp lactate sampling)
cohort: 600 pregnant women (300 Class III obese and 300 with normal BMI) planning a vaginal birth who had a live, singleton delivery from January 2015 to December 2018
finding: Class III obesity is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery, longer duration of labor in those who underwent induction, and higher rates of intrapartum interventions.
mod_finding: Class III obesity is associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
